paragraphs.text: وَيُطْعِمُونَ الطَّعَامَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ مِسْكِينًا وَيَتِيمًا وَأَسِيرًا

en.text: Source / locator: Qur’an, al-Insan, 76:8. Arabic and Jalandhari: SurahQuran; Pickthall: Quranic Arabic Corpus.
Published English excerpt: And feed with food the needy wretch, the orphan and the prisoner, for love of Him,
Verification / translation sources: Verified Arabic and published translation excerpts. English: Marmaduke Pickthall. Urdu: Fateh Muhammad Jalandhari.
Relevance: Names vulnerable recipients, including a captive. The principle is relevant to humane care without relying on an unverified anecdote about a particular recipient.

Context / qualification: The published translations resolve “ʿala hubbihi” differently: Pickthall connects it with love of Him; Jalandhari with the giver’s desire for food. Both are reproduced unchanged.
Best use: Argument
Verify:

Pickthall

Relevance: A direct warning concerning ihtikar. The surrounding report itself raises a question about storing goods; the term must not be expanded silently into a ban on every inventory or reserve.

Scholarly position / paraphrased argument: The commentary records both readings of “ʿala hubbihi”, preferring the reading that people give food despite wanting it themselves. It also records differing identifications of captives, including non-Muslims; it does not confine the discussion to one recipient group.

Verification / translation sources: Ibn Kathir (Abridged), English text on Quran.com, inspected at the verse-group and named passage. Compiler’s English–Urdu paraphrase; not a claim to have collated the complete Arabic edition.
Relevance: Explains the translation difference in the related Qur’anic entry and the wider humanitarian relevance of captive care.
Context / qualification: Reports about particular historical meals are not independently authenticated or separately counted in this entry.
Best use: Critical analysis / conceptual framework
Verify:
Source 1

en.text: Source / locator: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, “Great Mosque and Hospital of Divriği”, World Heritage List no. 358; Outstanding Universal Value: Brief synthesis, hospital paragraph, and criterion (iv). Accessed 18 September 2026.

Scholarly position / paraphrased argument: UNESCO’s detailed account identifies the adjoining dar al-shifa as a hospital founded by Turan Melek and designed by Hurrem Shah in 1228–1229. It describes the linked mosque–hospital complex, its internal spaces and the hospital’s charitable character.

Verification / translation sources: Official institutional essay or heritage statement inspected. The English and Urdu text is the compiler’s paraphrase of secondary historical analysis; no underlying manuscript or archaeological object was independently examined.
Relevance: A concrete institutional precedent linking worship, care, craft and a woman’s patronage; complements the general charity evidence without duplicating it.

Context / qualification: The detailed section distinguishes the hospital’s patron from the mosque’s. No claims about free treatment for every patient, clinical effectiveness or an inspected waqf deed are added.
Best use: Critical analysis / conceptual framework
Verify:
Source 1

ur.text: ماخذ / محل: یونیسکو عالمی ورثہ مرکز، «Great Mosque and Hospital of Divriği»، عالمی ورثہ فہرست نمبر 358؛ غیرمعمولی عالمی قدر: «Brief synthesis» میں ہسپتال کا پیراگراف اور معیار (iv)۔ رسائی: 18 ستمبر 2026۔
